title: I made a multilingual 21 questions style card game with Cursor
author: matteo101man
selftext:
[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/break-the-ice-peel/id6766398707](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/break-the-ice-peel/id6766398707)

I've always had trouble trying to figure out what to talk about when I meet new people for the first time, whether it's a conversation online or in-person, relationships and with friends.

To remedy this I sometimes will break out some 21 questions style card games you might see on the app store, which turn out to be really fun!

I thought to try with some of my knowledge using things like Cursor/Claude/Etc I might give it a try making my own version, and here I present to you my first app:

**Break the Ice - Peel**

  
**Workflow**

My whole workflow has pretty much just been using Cursor and its various models for image generation and coding, with Claude for some of the initial heavy lifting. I've also messed around with skills such as grill-me (https://www.skills.sh/mattpocock/skills/grill-me) which helped guide my ideas and GPT Image 2.0 to draft concepts (which i then took the reference images of and plugged back into cursor)

  
For serverside aspects, I just use google firebase.

  
**About**

Again it's based off of the 21 questions style, so there is different categories that you can choose from depending on what you want to talk about / how well you know the person you're talking to.

  
What makes it slightly different is you can play multiplayer and have a friend join you to play at a distance! and additionally it supports multiple languages. So perhaps if you may have a language barrier but want to learn more about someone you can enable the cards to have prompts in 2 target languages (supporting English, Japanese, Korean, Russian, & Mongolian currently). Even better, if you do opt for multiplayer mode there is an integrated chat system with google translate so you can translate answers back and forth!

The point is to try to keep the context the same across languages and really understand what someone is trying to tell you

Feel free to give it a try and tell me what you think! It's my first app so it could definitely use some work, but I'm open to suggestions.
